conversation.Statement: Hello, this is Brian Matthews from the IRS Tax Refund Department. I'm calling regarding your recent federal tax submission. Can I confirm I'm speaking with Alex Parker?
Yes, this is Alex. Did I do something wrong with my taxes?
No need to worry, Alex. In fact, according to our records, you actually qualify for a special refund under the recent stimulus adjustments. I just need to verify some details to process your payment.
Oh, a refund? That's great, I wasn't expecting that. What do you need from me?
We'll need to complete an identity verification protocol, as well as a small processing fee to unlock the release. The IRS requires these steps to prevent fraudulent claims.
A fee? I thought refunds just went into your account. Why do I have to pay?

Normally yes, but due to increased tax fraud attempts this year, the IRS has implemented a temporary $149 verification fee for first-time filers receiving unexpected refunds. Once cleared, your $2,800 refund will be directly deposited.
Uh, okay. I haven't heard of that before. How do I pay the fee?
For your convenience, we accept payment using Zelle or Cash App. Alternatively, you can purchase a set of prepaid Visa gift cards totaling $149 and provide the card numbers for instant processing.
Can't you just take it out of the refund? I don't really use Zelle or Cash App.

Unfortunately, IRS policy prohibits deduction from refunds for verification purposes. It must be completed before funds are released. If the fee isn't paid by close of business today, your refund will be canceled and flagged for further review.
Wait, it can be canceled? I don't want that to happen.
I understand your concern. It's important we act quickly because delays can also lead to a penalty review and possible suspension of future returns.
Alright. I guess I can get a prepaid Visa card at the pharmacy down the street?
Exactly. You can purchase one or several cards totaling $149. Once you have them, call this number back or stay on the line so I can process your verification and expedite your refund.
Is it safe to read card numbers over the phone like this?
Absolutely, this is the secure IRS processing line. Your information is never shared and is used solely for verification as required by IRS guidelines.
Okay, I'll go get the cards now. Should I stay on the line?

If you prefer, you can stay connected or call back in the next 20 minutes. Remember, if we don't complete the verification today, your refund will be automatically forfeited and you may be subject to further IRS investigation.
Oh, I really don't want that. I'll go get the cards and call you right back.
Perfect. Once you have the cards, just read the numbers from the front and back to me. I'll confirm your payment and provide a transaction code for your records.
